history.heading: Vikings and the medieval kingdom
paragraphs: Sweden has been inhabited since the end of the last Ice Age, and the Sámi have lived in the north for thousands of years. In the Viking Age, Swedish Vikings (Varangians) travelled east along Russian rivers to Constantinople and Baghdad, trading and founding settlements.

Sweden was gradually unified and Christianised from the 10th to 12th centuries. It joined the Kalmar Union with Denmark and Norway in 1397 but broke away in 1523 under Gustav Vasa, who founded the modern Swedish state and introduced Lutheranism.

history.heading: Great power era
paragraphs: In the 17th century, under Gustavus Adolphus, Sweden intervened in the Thirty Years' War and became a great power controlling much of the Baltic region. Its power ended with defeat by Russia in the Great Northern War (1700–1721). Sweden lost Finland to Russia in 1809.
Since 1814 Sweden has not fought a war, maintaining a long policy of neutrality. In the late 19th century, poverty led about a quarter of the population to emigrate, mostly to the United States.

history.heading: The Swedish model
paragraphs: In the 20th century Sweden industrialised and, under long Social Democratic rule, built an extensive welfare state known as the "Swedish model". It stayed neutral in both world wars. Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated in 1986. Sweden joined the EU in 1995 and, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, joined NATO in March 2024, ending two centuries of military non-alignment.

culture.heading: Society and values
paragraphs: Swedish is the official language, with recognised minority languages including Sámi and Finnish. Sweden is one of the most secular countries in the world, though many belong to the Church of Sweden. Values such as equality, consensus and lagom (moderation) are important.
Midsummer, Lucia Day (13 December) and fika, a coffee and pastry break, are cherished traditions. The Nobel Prizes, founded by Alfred Nobel, are awarded in Stockholm.

culture.heading: Culture and inventions
paragraphs: Sweden has produced ABBA, Avicii and many pop songwriters, writers Astrid Lindgren (Pippi Longstocking) and Selma Lagerlöf, filmmaker Ingmar Bergman, and crime fiction such as The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo. Swedish companies include IKEA, Volvo, Ericsson, H&M and Spotify. Food includes meatballs, herring, cinnamon buns and crispbread.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Sweden is a parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy; King Carl XVI Gustaf has a ceremonial role. The prime minister leads the government, responsible to the Riksdag, elected by proportional representation. Since 2022 a centre-right government has ruled with the support of the nationalist Sweden Democrats. Immigration, integration and gang violence have become major political issues.

economy.heading: Innovation economy
paragraphs: Sweden has a highly developed, export-oriented economy with strengths in engineering, telecoms, cars and trucks (Volvo, Scania), pharmaceuticals, forestry, steel, mining and music streaming. It is one of the world's most innovative economies and has produced many tech startups.
Sweden combines a market economy with high taxes and generous welfare. Nearly all electricity comes from nuclear and renewable sources. Sweden is nearly cashless. The currency is the Swedish krona.
